text: {"lessons":["Selling Stock A and D after gains felt rewarding, but my cost basis is not a sound reason by itself to sell; I should judge each holding by its role in the portfolio.","I added to Stock A, C and D, then watched the account decline. That does not prove the buys were wrong or predict a rebound; I should size positions for risk and avoid decisions driven by attachment to a purchase price.","With prices moving randomly and no need to trade often, I should review the whole portfolio calmly and trade only when a considered plan—not a short-term move or the urge to lock in gains—calls for it."]}
